description: Run a read-only SQL SELECT against OECD observation tables staged on a DataCanvas by oecd_query_dataset. Call oecd_dataframe_describe first to discover exact table and column names, then use this tool for aggregation, filtering, GROUP BY, JOIN, and window functions. Returns up to `limit` rows (default 100, at most 1,000 per call) and at most 1 MiB of row data; truncated: true marks a result with more rows than came back, and its notice says how to reach the rest. A query still running after 30 seconds is stopped. Unavailable when the server runs with DataCanvas disabled.

canvas_id.description: Canvas ID returned by oecd_query_dataset — exactly 10 characters of letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores. Identifies the DataCanvas session holding the observation tables.

limit.description: Most rows to return. Default 100; served up to 1,000 per call, so a value from 1,001 to 10,000 returns at most 1,000 rows and a notice saying so. Fewer come back when the rows would pass 1 MiB of row data. For more rows than one call returns, aggregate in SQL or page with ORDER BY … LIMIT … OFFSET.

sql.description: Read-only SELECT statement. Reference tables by the names returned by oecd_dataframe_describe. Only SELECT statements are allowed — DDL, DML, and file-reading functions are rejected.

name: oecd_dataframe_query

column_names.description: Column names in the result, in order.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `canvas_disabled`: DataCanvas is not configured — CANVAS_PROVIDER_TYPE=none. `canvas_not_found`: The canvas_id has expired or was never created. `table_not_found`: The SQL names a table this canvas does not hold — it expired, was dropped, or the name is wrong. `invalid_sql`: The SQL is not a valid SELECT statement or contains disallowed operations. `sql_execution_error`: The SQL parsed and ran, then failed on the staged observation data — a conversion, an invalid input, or a value out of range. `query_timeout`: The query was still running after 30 seconds and was stopped. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

notice.description: Present when a requested limit was above the per-call maximum (naming the limit requested and the one served), or when truncated is true (naming the ways to reach the rows not returned).

row_count.description: Number of rows returned — the length of rows, never the size of the full result.

rows.description: Result rows in query order: at most limit rows (1,000 per call) and at most 1 MiB of row data. When truncated is true the result has more rows than these.

truncated.description: True when the result has more rows than this call returned — cut at limit or at the 1 MiB row-data budget; the notice says how to reach the rest. Omitted (never false) when rows is the complete result.

title: Oecd Dataframe Query
